solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soft-hearted money-lenders making pretence a reality

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for people who do this; the answer is a plural noun

indicators.note: something at the heart of a thing sits in its middle, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: usurers lend money at excessive interest
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Kindly moneylenders who somehow turn a pretence into something real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft-hearted' reads as kindly, but it means P placed in the heart of USURERS. A pretender claims a throne; a usurper actually takes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurper seizes a position or throne he only claimed, turning a pretender's claim into actual power.

clue.text: US writer rising to Holland's defence

parts.note: something rising goes up
the Dutch hold back the sea with dikes

explanation.surface: An American author springs up to defend the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' in a down clue looks like a reversal signal, but here it simply supplies its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: John Updike was the American novelist famous for the Rabbit books and many New Yorker stories.

clue.text: A bilingual graduate dropped but still confident

parts.note: una is the word for 'a' in both Spanish and Italian
a Bachelor of Arts is a graduate
to shed something is to drop it

explanation.surface: A graduate who speaks two languages got thrown out yet stays self-assured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bilingual' tells you to translate 'A' into a form shared by two languages, Spanish and Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unabashed is not embarrassed or put off, so they remain assured and bold.

clue.text: Hotel employees a long time in extra thought

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a postscript is a thought added at the end of a letter
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Hotel staff spend ages over an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: PS, the postscript, is a common crossword stand-in for an afterthought.
explanation.definitionFit: Pages are young uniformed attendants in grand hotels who run errands and carry messages for guests.

clue.text: Sends back the proceeds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, gives or dispatches something back
second meaning: a noun, the profit an investment yields

explanation.surface: Someone returns the money a sale made.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one action on the proceeds; it is two separate senses of the same word, verb then noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for giving something back and as a noun for income produced by an investment.

clue.text: Stolen gun and car

parts.note: stolen goods are called hot
rod is American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: A list of a criminal's loot: a stolen gun and a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface lists two stolen items, but 'Stolen' and 'gun' combine to name the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-rod is an ordinary car modified with a boosted engine for speed and acceleration.

clue.text: Superintends, but misses something

definitions.meaning: first meaning: supervises, keeps watch over

explanation.surface: A supervisor who oversees everything and still misses something.
explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are nearly opposite: watching over versus failing to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee a workplace is one sense; failing to notice an error is the other sense of the same verb.

clue.text: Wine jar I smashed when empty

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into pieces that can be put back in any order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
empty means holding nothing, and nothing is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to breaking the wine jar once it had been drunk dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' seems to describe the jar, but it adds an O, zero, to the letters being broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Reduce police force in naval establishment

parts.note: to dock pay is to reduce it
the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Cutting the police presence at a navy base.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard, the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, is often just 'the Yard'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dockyard is where naval ships are built, repaired and fitted out, often run by the navy.

clue.text: Checkers of medical doses

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the board game Americans call checkers
second meaning: measured drinks of medicine

explanation.surface: People who check how much medicine is given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checkers' looks like inspectors; it is the American name for the British board game.
explanation.definitionFit: The British name for the board game checkers, and also old-fashioned word for a liquid dose of medicine.

clue.text: Undaunted, he leads or retreats in command

indicators.note: to lead is to go first, so this piece starts the word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so these letters run the other way

parts.note: taken as written
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge or in command

explanation.surface: A fearless commander either leads from the front or pulls back.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets leading against retreating as a battlefield choice; both words are instructions for the small words around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic behaviour is brave and unflinching, showing courage that fear cannot shake.

clue.text: Novice Tory is replaced

indicators.note: when letters are replaced they are put back in new positions

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new Conservative MP is swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party; here it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a beginner or learner, someone with little experience in a field.

clue.text: Poet takes orders

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet takes holy orders, or accepts instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes orders' reads as a phrase about obeying or ordination; the verb 'orders' acts on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was the English Romantic poet who wrote the great odes.

clue.text: Sailors in two shades of blue

parts.note: royal blue is the first shade, a bright deep blue
navy blue is the second shade, a very dark blue

explanation.surface: Seamen dressed in uniforms of two different blues.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures sailors in uniform; the two named colours simply join end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Navy is Britain's naval force, whose members are sailors.

clue.text: He had doubts and got zero in maths revision

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within another
a revision reworks material, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A student had misgivings and scored nothing in his maths revision.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a student's exam gloom; 'revision' is the rearranging signal, not studying.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubting Thomas was the apostle who would not believe in the resurrection until he saw the wounds.

clue.text: Looking shabby, he meant to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters take a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; the word also belongs to the indicator phrase

explanation.surface: A scruffy man intended to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' does double duty: it is part of the letters to shuffle and also reads as part of 'to reform'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes chewed by moths look worn and full of holes, hence the adjective for anything tatty or run-down.

clue.text: Small number return present — now available at reduced price

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: no. is the short form of number
to present something is to offer it

explanation.surface: A shop sells a few returned gifts at a discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' tells you to shorten number to its abbreviation. 'Return present' sounds like taking back a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods on offer in a British shop are being sold at a special discounted price.

clue.text: There's worse to come out of this

definitions.text: There's worse to come out of this

parts.note: surface reading: a gloomy warning that a bad situation will get worse
setter's reading: the kitchen utensil you jump from into the fire, in the proverb

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'out of the frying pan into the fire' means escaping one trouble only to land in a worse one.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names this cooking vessel as the lesser danger that you leave only to fall into the fire.

clue.text: Note smoker in pub is a musician

indicators.note: being in a place means being inside it, so these pieces go within another

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a pipe is something smoked
G is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: The man smoking in the pub turns out to be a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoker' suggests a person, but here it is the thing smoked.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagpiper plays the bagpipes, the Scottish wind instrument, so is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Checked the accuracy of others' accounts?

definitions.text: Checked the accuracy of others' accounts?

parts.words: Checked the accuracy of others' accounts
parts.note: surface reading: verified the stories other people told
setter's reading: accounts as financial records, examined by an accountant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Accounts' first suggests stories or versions of events; the question mark flags the bookkeeping sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of a company's financial records by an independent accountant.

clue.text: Expected to end in mortal combat

parts.note: something due is expected

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fight was always going to end in death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mortal combat' reads as one phrase, but 'mortal' only supplies a letter and 'combat' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal fight between two people, a kind of single combat.

clue.text: Chump about to declare in tests

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to say is to declare

explanation.surface: A fool is about to announce the results of his exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of'; split it, and 'about' wraps the fool round 'to declare'.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is a test of a metal or substance to determine its quality or composition.

clue.text: Old Greek hunter made to work to a great age

parts.note: to act is to work or function
taken as written
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek huntsman forced to keep working into old age.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hunter working until old; the pieces are a verb, the article and a long period.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Actaeon was the hunter turned into a stag by Artemis and killed by his own hounds.

clue.text: In class it's hard to be virtuous

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one letter goes within the word

parts.note: a caste is a social class
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: In a school class, it is hard to behave well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' suggests a schoolroom but means a social rank; 'it's' reads as 'it is' and is only filler.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means morally pure, particularly abstaining from sex, so it is a kind of virtue.

clue.text: Past example to go in front of book

parts.note: to precede is to go before
NT, the New Testament, is a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: An earlier case placed at the front of a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' is often NT or OT, the Testaments of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A precedent is an earlier case or decision used as a guide or model for later ones.

clue.text: Choose to take part in college lectures

indicators.note: taking part of something means using only a portion, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A student decides to join in the lectures at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take part in' sounds like participating, but it asks for a part of the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to pick someone or something by vote or decision, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Drink provided for horse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mixed drink of fruit juice and spirits served from a bowl
second meaning: a heavy English carthorse breed from Suffolk

explanation.surface: Someone lays out a drink for a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Suffolk Punch is a breed of English carthorse, often just called a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fruity party beverage and a stocky breed of working carthorse.

clue.text: Leapt out from the crease

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A batsman jumped out of his crease.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the line a cricket batsman stands behind; 'leapt out from the crease' is a batting image, but here the crease is a fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold pressed or stitched into fabric, a deliberate crease in cloth.

clue.text: Preston North End exited rapidly

indicators.note: the end has left, so a letter at the tail is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: The football club Preston North End went out of a competition quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Preston North End is an English football club; the name is broken up so that the north letter at the end leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction for a very fast tempo, and also means quickly in general.

clue.text: Set price being fixed, proceeds

indicators.note: something fixed has been repaired or rigged, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fixed price, once agreed, lets a sale go ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' looks like a verb meaning goes on, but it is the noun for money taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Receipts are the money taken in by a business, its takings or income from sales.

clue.text: Grade scrap metal inside

indicators.note: something inside another thing is enclosed by it

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Sort the scrap metal kept indoors by quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap metal' reads as one thing, but it splits into a scrap of cloth and a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a grade or classification awarded according to standard or quality.

clue.text: An insect's metamorphosis, for example

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a complete change of form, so the letters take a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A caterpillar becoming a butterfly, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: An insect's metamorphosis is the textbook example of change, which is exactly what the letters undergo.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or illustration, as in the phrase for instance.
